Whether or not my workflow is productive and how I can increase my productivity has been a popular topic in my head this past year. I have a naturally inefficient productivity ratio of time spent to results produced and a decent portion of this year has been devoted to improving that ratio. So far, after going through many systems of variety, the ratio has increased only slightly. I believe it can only increase slightly over long periods of time, so patience and perseverance has been my strategy of choice.

I am a systems-based person, so anything I can automate I try to automate. This includes backups, email, grocery shopping, publishing certain types of media, etc. Being a system-based person also means I completely abhor tedious tasks. In terms of my computer life, my essential tools regarding automation/productivity include:

  • FreeFileSync — My go-to sync tool
  • Task Scheduler — Automates backups and file purges with FreeFileSync and batch files
  • WinSCP — Automates remote file access and backups
  • FileZilla Server — Hosts remote files
  • Bulk Rename Utility — Automates file renaming
  • DisplayFusion — Quick to-system tray, window transparency, and other shortcuts
  • Everything — Windows search alternative with better indexing and utility
  • Greenshot — Screenshot tool with quick actions
  • MediaFire Desktop — Sync tool (backups)
  • Microsoft OneDrive — Sync tool (backups)
  • Microsoft OneNote — Notes organizer and journal system
  • Microsoft Outlook — Email and Calendar client with automation capability
  • Wunderlist — Task and to-do organizer
  • AutoHotkey — Scripting tool
  • Syncthing — Sync tool (backups)
  • Batch files — Scripting
  • Lastpass — Password manager that syncs to all my devices and browsers with autofill and password generation
  • Pomodoro — time management app using the Pomodoro Technique
  • and Price Zombie — Price comparison with useful automated emails

Though my workflow has been influenced by an uncountable number of resources online, the biggest influences I credit to would be CGP Grey on the Hello Internet and Cortex podcasts.

Finally, my questions for the community here is as follows:

  • Would you consider yourself an efficient or productive worker?
  • Do you use any tools to help? If so, what tools?
  • For other system-based people: would you be so kind and let a noob in on some tips you've learned? :-)
Would you consider yourself productive with your general tasks?

Would you consider yourself an efficient or productive worker?

I manage to be, in spite of myself. I couldn't tell how precisely, the fact that I can stay focus 12 hours working on the same thing with very few breaks helps.

Also, before actually beginning a new task, I can spend a long time reading about it, then experimenting (trial-an-error). This makes working very slow the first couple of days, then productivity skyrockets.

Do you use any tools to help? If so, what tools?

If I need some part of my work automated, I write a script for it. But, in opposition to you, I like to retain (a perceived) control of most tasks.

What really speeds up my work is the quality of the tools. For example, I've started using new IDEs and exploring their possibilities, it makes a very big difference when they are capable of simplifying and automating small but complex tasks.

I consider myself a productive worker if I'm motivated in the task I'm working on. Sometimes I get sidetracked or lose interest, but most of the time I believe I'm fairly productive. I admit I'm always looking for ways to be more efficient, especially with my time, as sometimes I'll finish a task only to realize there was an easier, more efficient alternative method I could have used. It's definitely something I can always improve upon.
